text:
We were cutting down the trees with high explosives' cordate. I had a belt clip of of dynamite caps, somehow I had dropped one of the dynamite caps and was carrying one to me. Well the heat of the hand, it will go off, it's that sensitive. He had no idea what it was. He picked it up and was bringing it to me and it blew some fingers off. I felt so sorry for him. We were keeping his arms up to prevent his blood from pumping out. Anyways, we got him to the Vietnamese army hospital. When we left, I thought he's Cambodian and the hospital isn't going to help him. It added PTSD. I wasn't able to go back because we were flying away. Do they have a Cambodian area in there with Cambodian nurses?

Location: Nui Ba Den, down by the helicopter pad. The hospital was in Saigon by Ton Suhn Nhut. We landed and some ARVN (army republic of Vietnam) nurses came out. Being American, I don't think we could go in. The nurses came out and took him.

timeframe: Jan/Feb/Mar of 1965

The picture is him in the helicopter laying on the back floor. 
I didn't know him very well. This is a different Cambodian than the one always hanging out with me.
